RetailCo Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the RetailCo Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss RetailCo Inc.'s results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; and Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Jonathan Hale.

Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report RetailCo Inc.'s performance for the Q2 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover four key aspects of our performance:

1. Key assumptions underlying guidance. Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, thank you for being with us on RetailCo's second quarter earnings call. Before we get into questions later, let me outline our full-year fiscal 2024 guidance and the core assumptions behind it. As you know, we're targeting consolidated net sales of $28.5 billion to $29.0 billion, which translates to 3% to 5% growth year-over-year, with comparable store sales—or comps—in the 2% to 4% range. Adjusted operating income is set at $1.8 billion to $1.95 billion, implying EBITDA margins of 8.5% to 9.0%, an improvement of about 20 to 50 basis points from fiscal 2023. Diluted EPS guidance stands at $2.45 to $2.65.

These targets stem from our disciplined approach in a resilient yet uneven retail landscape, where our brick-and-mortar stores anchor omnichannel experiences even as inflation moderates and consumers spend selectively. Let me detail the key assumptions, grouped into macroeconomic conditions, consumer patterns, operational improvements, and strategic efforts.

First, on the macroeconomic front, we're projecting U.S. GDP growth to ease to 2.0% to 2.2% for calendar 2024, aligning with Fed projections and estimates from the Conference Board. Consumer confidence, per the University of Michigan index, should stay around 70-75, bolstered by real wage increases of 1.5% to 2.0% year-over-year, while headline CPI drops to 2.5% by year-end. Unemployment is expected to remain low at 4.1% to 4.3%, supporting our primary customers—middle-income households aged 35-54, who account for 65% of apparel and home goods sales.

Cost-wise, freight and logistics inflation is forecasted at 1% to 2%, a sharp drop from over 15% in 2022, due to stabilized transpacific rates and full Panama Canal operations after the drought. Energy expenses, including diesel for our 1,200-store delivery fleet, are flat to down 5%, with WTI crude averaging $75-80 per barrel. Interest rates for the 10-year Treasury peak in the mid-5% range before declining 25-50 basis points in Q4, aiding our $2.5 billion revolving credit facility priced at LIBOR plus 175 basis points. Regionally, we're bullish on the Sunbelt, with Southeast and Southwest comps potentially at 4% to 6%, driven by population growth and home formation 20% above national averages per Census figures. We're more conservative in the Northeast and Midwest, where comps might hit 0% to 2%, impacted by sluggish housing and office vacancies at 18-20%, similar to issues at Macy's and Kohl's.

Second, consumer behavior and traffic: Store traffic is assumed to fall mid-single digits, around 4% to 6%, matching Placer.ai data showing visits still 10-15% below 2019 levels. Yet our comps include a 300-500 basis point conversion boost from promotions and loyalty personalization. Average ticket rises 1% to 2%, thanks to better attachment on big-ticket home items like our expanded Martha Stewart kitchen collections, which posted +12% comps in Q2.

E-commerce penetration holds at 22% to 24% of sales, off pandemic highs of 28% but up from 20% in 2023, with BOPIS handling 45% of online orders—a 25% YoY jump. No big stimulus pull-forward expected, but tailwinds from back-to-school and holidays could push apparel comps over 5% if weather aligns with NOAA patterns. Inventory turns accelerate to 5.2x annually from 4.8x trailing twelve months, optimized by AI assortment planning that cuts markdowns 150 basis points.

Shrink improves 20 basis points to 1.6% of sales via RFID tagging in 60% of stores by year-end, akin to Home Depot's pilots reducing losses 30%. We're realistic about urban theft in our 150 downtown lifestyle locations.

Third, operational efficiencies and margins: Gross margins expand 40-60 basis points to 38.5% to 39.0%, from 100 basis points in sourcing savings as Vietnam and Bangladesh factories increase output 15%, lower cotton prices down 10% YoY per ICAC, and freight gains from our new 1.2 million square foot automated Memphis DC launching in Q3. Promo intensity remains at 22% of sales, below the 25% NRF industry average.

SG&A deleverages 10-20 basis points to 29.5% to 30.0% of sales, with payroll steady at 85,000 full-time equivalents despite 5% square footage growth from remodels, and rent growth at 2% after renewing 75% of leases below market post-COVID. Capex guidance is $850 million, or 3% of sales: 40% for store remodels including 100 small-format express stores in exurban areas, 30% for supply chain like micro-fulfillment with Alert Innovation following Walmart's model, 20% for IT via MACH architecture upgrade, and 10% maintenance.

Fourth, strategic moves and risks: This includes 'Store of the Future' in 200 locations with experiential zones like interactive beauty bars and AR-fitted apparel, similar to Nordstrom, generating 2x traffic in pilots. Plan for 10-15 closures of small underperformers, offset by 20 new Sunbelt openings in high-barrier markets with strong demographics. Our NextGen loyalty app has 18 million active users up 22% YoY, driving 60% of comps with Adobe Experience Cloud and Snowflake personalization. Canadian 50 stores flat to +2% comps at CAD/USD 0.73, no USMCA tariffs.

Risks include unemployment over 4.5%, Red Sea freight spikes adding 5-10%, or weather issues; upsides from private label at 45%, or +1% comps if gas under $3.50/gallon. We'll update as we go—this shows faith in our omnichannel edge.

2. Earnings guidance for next quarter/year. Thank you. Good morning, everyone, for our Q2 earnings call at RetailCo Inc. Before Q&A, here's our outlook for Q3 and full fiscal 2024, building on our "Store Forward" strategy in a steady but cautious consumer setting.

For Q3, consolidated net sales should range $7.125 billion to $7.25 billion, up 2% to 5% YoY. This factors SSS growth of 1.5% to 4%, from seasonal back-to-school and early holiday setups, offsetting last year's easy post-pandemic comps. Digital sales at 18% of revenue—up from 15% last year—expect high-single-digit growth via BOPIS at record 65% of e-comm in Q2.

Adjusted diluted EPS guided to $1.45 to $1.65, up 5% to 15% from last Q3. Gross margins at 37.2% to 37.7%, expanding 20-70 bps on supply chain gains from Atlanta and Dallas micro-fulfillment cutting out-of-stocks 25%, and mix to higher-margin hardlines like paint and tools up 8% in Q2, tracking Home Depot and Lowe's.

SG&A at 24.5% to 25.0% of sales, via AI workforce tools like Walmart's reducing overtime 12% YTD. Adjusted EBITDA margins 11.0% to 11.5%, backing $450 million share repurchases.

For full FY2024, raising midpoint: net sales $28.5 billion to $29.0 billion, 3% to 5% growth, SSS 2.5% to 4.5%. Adjusted EPS $5.80 to $6.20, up 7% to 14%, gross margins up 50-100 bps to 37.0% to 37.5%.

Drivers: remodeling 150 big-box stores with "Essentials Kitchen" zones boosting conversions 15%, plus 20 new urban small-formats in Chicago and Miami. Capex $850 million to $900 million, 60% supply chain including RFID in 40% of 1,200 stores like Target's accuracy boosts.

Regionally, Sunbelt SSS 5% to 7% in Q3 on migration and renos; Northeast/Midwest flat to 2% from weather and discretionary pullback per Nielsen's 3% durables drop.

Omnichannel via "Seamless Essentials" with Instacart for same-day in 80% DMAs drove 20% digital comps in Q2. Private label ValueForge at 28% sales by year-end adds 300 bps margins from Vietnam/Mexico sourcing. Sustainability lumber up 12%, Gen Z 25% traffic.

Risks: sticky 3.2% core CPI, auto strikes; inventory-to-sales 11.2x down 150 bps YTD. Holiday ready with vendor markdowns, app notifications for 10% traffic. Assumes stable FX/tariffs; 45%+ adjusted net income to shareholders.

3. Omnichannel initiatives progress (e.g., BOPIS, curbside pickup). Thank you, and good morning. As part of Q3 results discussion, let's highlight omnichannel progress, central to our transformation at RetailCo with over 1,200 stores in 42 states as our moat. Seamlessly blending digital—now 28% of revenue up from 19% YoY—via BOPIS and curbside drives higher margins, traffic, retention versus Amazon's online-only.

Digital orders up 32% YoY to $1.2 billion in Q3, omnichannel (BOPIS/curbside) 62% or $745 million, +45% YoY. BOPIS orders +28% to 4.2 million units, 18% of digital vs 12% last year; success 98.2% via real-time inventory sync in 95% stores. AOV $85 up 12% in apparel/home.

Curbside +51% to 2.8 million, 70%+ from loyalty members with 22% higher repeats. Holiday peaks 25% of digital in dense markets like Target Drive Up. Margins +450 bps at 42.1% vs shipped, using store labor.

Tech: $45 million YTD in Omnichannel Orchestration Engine with Manhattan Associates/Google Cloud for SKU-level visibility, -37% stockouts. "Reserved In-Store" for Apple Watch/Dyson +19% conversions; Zebra scanners <2 min BOPIS; ShipStation for hybrid.

Regional: Northeast/Midwest urban (Chicago/NYC/Boston) 70%+ omni penetration, BOPIS +35%, Michigan Ave +15% SSS halo. Sunbelt curbside 45%, rural up 40% via Grocity micro-fulfillment.

De-risks macro: Q3 comps +4.2%, 1.8 pts omni halo; omni LTV 2.7x higher. Targeting 25% omni mix FY25 with AR apparel Snapchat, vendor-direct BOPIS. Wins via store arbitrage.

4. Digital marketing effectiveness. Good afternoon, everyone—joining RetailCo Holdings' Q2 call, omnichannel leader in home furnishings/lifestyle with 1,200 North American/European stores. Diving into digital marketing, our top-ROI lever—not just e-comm but traffic/BOPIS for physical moats vs Wayfair/Amazon. Contributed 28% revenue growth via "Digital-to-Door."

Q2 spend $48.2 million +18% YoY, 12% SG&A; ROAS 5.8x best in 3 years vs Home Depot 4.9x/Macy's 4.2x = $280 million sales. Performance media (Google/Meta/TikTok) 62% at 7.2x; brand YouTube/CTV 3.1x.

Attribution via GA4/Tealium CDP multi-touch: captures Instagram-to-Google-to-BOPIS; digital influences 65% in-store buys +17% vs last year. Placer.ai: +22% visits, 14% conversion.

CAC -11% to $28, LTV/CAC 3.7x, LTV $215 vs RH >$40.

AI personalization: Performance Max 2.0 on 75% portfolio +34% CTR/19% conv via 42M loyalty data; Adobe Sensei Meta variants for rugs.

Geofencing 2,500 rivals (IKEA/Pottery Barn) 4.2x ROAS, 8% BOPIS; Dallas +31% traffic.

Privacy: server-side Google Tag/Consent v2 recovers 85% iOS loss; zero-party quizzes 15M profiles, Trade Desk CPM -17% to $12.50.

U.S. 6.4x ROAS (SE 7.1x outdoor; MW 4.9x weather counter; NE TikTok 9.2%); Europe 4.2x on $9.8M, Criteo contextual +28%, influencers +42% youth.

55% performance/45% brand; proximity scoring 2.5x ROAS boost, +5.2% SSS vs NRF +2.8%.

Q3: RMN "RetailCo Ads" P&G $20M 8x; TikTok 40%; Snapchat AR 15% BOPIS; Amazon DSP diversify. Raising FY24 ROAS 5.5x-6.0x for 8-10% growth. Digital as traffic engine.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Rivera to provide more details on our financial results.

Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Jonathan. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q2 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $7.15 billion, a 4.2% increase compared to the same period last year, driven by solid comps of 3.1% and digital growth. Gross margin came in at 38.4%, primarily driven by sourcing efficiencies from Asian partners, lower commodity costs like cotton, and optimized freight from our new DCs. Operating expenses were $2.11 billion, representing 29.5% of revenue, reflecting payroll discipline and lease renewals. Net income was $480 million, or $0.92 per share. We generated $720 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently well-controlled, turning at 5.1x annualized, with units per store optimized through AI planning.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, instructions for questions... Our first question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of moderating inflation on your sales?

Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, Emily. Moderating inflation has been a net positive, supporting real wage growth for our core middle-income demo and keeping consumer confidence stable around 70-75 per Michigan data. We've seen selective spending lift average tickets 1-2%, especially in home categories, though traffic pressures persist. Our guidance embeds CPI cooling to 2.5%, aiding comps without aggressive promos.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Patel (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, David. For Q3, we're looking at SSS of 1.5% to 4%, incorporating seasonal lifts from back-to-school and holidays, balanced against last year's comps. Sunbelt strength at 5-7% offsets softer Northeast/Midwest, with omnichannel halo adding 1-2 points.

Operator:
Our next question is from Lisa Ramirez with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Ramirez (Morgan Stanley):
Thanks. On omnichannel, how sustainable is the BOPIS growth, and any updates on micro-fulfillment?

Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer:
Great question, Lisa. BOPIS at 18% of digital is very sustainable, with 98% fulfillment and rising AOV to $85. Our new micro-centers in Atlanta/Dallas and Texas/Florida pilots are reducing stockouts 25-37%, scaling to more stores and targeting sub-2-hour options. This drives 450 bps margin accretion and halo traffic.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes questions at this time.

Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
